1. Acquire copper wire, though any (not very corrosive) metal will do: stainless steel, gold, silver, aluminum. For this wire I cut down my neighbours telephone line and stripped it.

  2. Create the pendant, to do this wrap a somewhat loose ball of wire, loose enough that you can later stick wires through it, dont worry if it feels it will fall apart. Now poke the end of the wire through the ball and pull it to create the petal shapes, try to stay on an "equatorial" line of the ball so it looks like a flower. then ensure that there is enough wire left (about a foot) for the next part.

  3. Create the chain. To make a chain piece, make a tight loop like a hairpin, then double back. Do this 4 times so that you have 2 loops on either side of a rod of wire. Then take that wire and wrap it around the center rod piece. Flange out the loops to create two intersecting loops on either side.

  4. Every chain piece created from now on will be connected to the previous one. It should be connected through BOTH loops on the last chain piece.

  5. Create a chain piece attached to the pendant using the spare foot of wire you had left. Obviously it needs to be connected to the center of the whole necklace.

  6. To create the clasp at the back of the necklace, simple bend the loops into tight hooks, if you make them tight enough it wont come off.
